2 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors 1. BRIEF FACTS/CASE OF THE CLAIMANT(s)
1.
In present case, FIR bearing no. 50/2015 was registered in PS Tilak Marg, Delhi on the complaint made by complaint Mohd. Khusbudin against driver Anil S/o Hawa Singh R-1.

A charge sheet was filed by the police against the driver Mr. Anil S/o Sh. Hawa Singh / R-1 under Section 279/338 IPC,
on the charges of rash driving of vehicle no. DL -1LG-0994 due to which injured Khushbuddin who was driving the motorcycle bearing no. DL7SAS -7464 suffered grievous injuries.
2. As per the DAR, the vehicle was driven by respondent no. 1 driver, owned by respondent no 2 and insured by respondent no. 3 Insurance company.
3. In present case the vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 i.e. Department of Posts Dak Bhawan New Delhi.

entities.text: Department of Posts Dak Bhawan New Delhi
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: R-1 and R-2 filed their written statement as well as written submissions.
As the vehicle was belonging to Government there is no insurance of the vehicle.
4. During the proceedings issues were framed on 15.03.2018 Thereafter the written submissions were filed by the parties in the prescribed format.

2. FRAMING OF ISSUES 5. Vide order dated 15.03.2018, following issues were framed by this Tribunal:-
DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 4 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors "1.
Whether

the .petitioner sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 14.02.2015 at about 8:10 a.m at Tilak Marg,
Opposite A Gate, Supreme Court of India, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1LG -0994 driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no. 2 ?

PW 1/ 2; copy of admission in Max Health Care Super Speciality Hospital along with bills paid to the hospital and other bills regarding medicines and treatment along with discharge summary are Ex. In his testimony PW-1 stated that on 14.02.2015 at around 8:10 p.m he was going to his home by riding his motor cycle bearing no. DL7SAS -7464.
When he reached gate no. 8 of Supreme Court of India, a vehicle bearing no. DL -1LG-0994 belonging to postal department tried to overtake his motorcycle and hit him.
Due to the impact he sustained grievous injuries and was taken to LNJP hospital.
Thereafter, he was moved to MAX Healthcare Super Speciality Hospital and remained hospitalized from 15.02.2015 to 20.02.2015.
Thereafter his out patient continued on regular basis.
He stated that he was working as a contractor for white washing in high rise building and was earing around Rs. 25,000/- per month.
9. Respondent examined RW-1 Mr. Anil Kumar was the driver of the offending vehicle.

Mr. Anil Kumar in his testimony stated that on 14.02.2015 he ws performing govt. duty while driving vehicle no. DL-1LG-0994 and was turning the vehicle form Tilak Marg to Supreme Court at a very slow speed and suddenly realized that something had hit the vehicle from back side.
He stopped the vehicle and went back and saw that a motorcycle had hit on the rear side of his vehicle.
He stated that injured Khushbuddin was driving his vehicle in rash manner and accident occurred due to his negligence.
DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 6 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors
4. ARGUMENTS OF COUNSELS OF THE PARTIES 10.Ld.
Counsel for the claimant contended that the accident occurred due to the wanton negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
He submitted that the factum of filing of charge sheet itself establishes negligence on the part of the driver.
11.He submitted that the injured was working as a painter and was earning around Rs. 20,000/- per month, but to cut short the controversy the minimum wages for unskilled worker may be considered.
Counsel for the R-1 and R-2 submitted that accident occurred due to rash driving of injured.
It is stated that the injured had given contradictory testimony and the respondents are not liable to pay the compensation.

5. ISSUE WISE ANALYSIS & FINDINGS THERETO (a) Issue No.1: Whether claimant sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on account of rash and negligent driving by the respondent driver?
i. Presumption qua complicity upon filing chargesheet:
13.

In a recent order dated 25.02.2025, passed in Ranjeet & Anr v Abdul Nayem Keb & Anr in SLP 10351/2019 , it was held in trenchant terms as thus:
Khushbuddin vs Anil Kumar (Govt. Vehicle) on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137585863/
4

entities.text: Ranjeet & Anr v Abdul Nayem Keb & Anr in SLP 10351/2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 7 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors

"It is settled in law that once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Even if the eyewitnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the bus driver."
14.In the present case, not only the FIR was registered and charge sheet was filed qua respondent no 1 driver u/s 279/338 IPC in the Court.
Thus, a presumption of negligence exists qua the driver respondent.
15.In addition to aforesaid, PW-1 injured in his testimony categorically stated that the accident occurred when the offending vehicle rashly tried to overtake his motorcycle and hit him.

The driver of offending vehicle is RW-1 Mr. Anil Kumar is his cross examination admitted that at the relevant point of time he had to apply sudden break as the vehicle in front of him suddenly stopped, due to which the victim's motorcycle which was driven behind him collided with his vehicle.

16.In addition to aforesaid, RW-1 driver Mr. Anil Kumar in his testimony also admitted that he was forced to drive beyond his duty hours of eight hours and on the date of accident he was doing second duty i.e the duty beyond eight hours.
driver in his affidavit admitted that on Tilak Marg he was taking a right turn towards the Supreme Court.

It is pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the claimant that the said cut DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 8 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors is meant for the Hon'ble Judges entry and not for any public vehicle.
To the contrary, RW-1 in his cross examination also admitted that at the point where accident took place, there was no place either to take turn or U-turn. RW-1
driving
in his cross examination admitted that he was driving on this route for the first time and was guided about the route by an official of postal department who was accompanying him.
The said fact is also clear from the site plan filed along with the charge sheet.

18. Therefore, from the material on record, it is clear that the firstly the offending vehicle was taking right cut from an unauthorized point and secondly the offending vehicle had applied sudden break which led to the accident.
The fact that the the driver was doing duty beyond his working hours cannot be ignored as the fatigue may impact driver's concentration and agility.

ii. Preponderance of probabilities:
19.It is trite law that in a proceeding before the Claims Tribunal, the claimant does not have to establish negligence on the part of the driver respondent beyond reasonable doubt.
The standards of establishing negligence is predicated on preponderance of probabilities.
In the present case too, negligence has been established on this principle.

In this context, it would be useful to peruse Mathew Alexander v. Mohd. Shafi,
(2023) 13 SCC 510 wherein it was observed as thus:
"In this context, we could refer to the judgments of this Court in N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd.
v. M. Karumai Ammal [N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M. Karumai Ammal, (1980) 3 SCC 457 : 1980 SCC (Cri) 774] , wherein the plea that the criminal case had ended in acquittal and that, therefore, the civil suit must follow suit, was rejected.

Similarly, in Bimla Devi v. Himachal RTC [Bimla Devi v. Himachal RTC, (2009) 13 SCC 530 : (2009) 5 SCC (Civ) 189 : (2010) 1 SCC (Cri)
1101] ("Bimla Devi"), it was observed that in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Tribunal has to determine the amount of fair compensation to be granted in the event an accident has taken place by reason of negligence of a driver of a motor vehicle.

sentences.text: A holistic view of the evidence has to be taken into consideration by the Tribunal and strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner need not be established by the claimants.
The claimants have to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt cannot be applied while considering the petition seeking compensation on account of death or injury in a road traffic accident.

To the same effect is the observation made by this Court in Dulcina Fernandes v. Joaquim Xavier Cruz [Dulcina Fernandes v. Joaquim Xavier Cruz, (2013) 10 SCC 646 : (2014) 1 SCC (Civ) 73 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri)
13] which has referred to the aforesaid judgment in Bimla DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 10 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors Devi [Bimla Devi v. Himachal RTC (2009) 13 SCC 530."

iii. Finding:
21.In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL1LG- 0994 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2.
Hence, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.

(b) Issue No.2: Whether claimant is entitled to compensation, and to what amount?
i. Extent of disability:
22. No disability is claimed in the present case by the injured.
ii. Principles qua assessment of compensation:

Before adverting to the submissions of the counsels in this regard, it would be apposite to refer to the law of the land qua this aspect.

The law has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 .

sentences.text: The gist DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 11 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
24. In Raj Kumar v Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 the heads under which compensation is to be calculated was expounded as thus :

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "5.The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some DAR No. 781/2017 Page.
12 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

[See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .]"

"6.The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 13 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii),
(v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life."
25.The claimant filed prescribed of the Scheme for Motor Accident Claims qua the above heads pertaining to pecuniary and non pecuniary damages.
26. Though the judgment of Raj Kumar (supra) deals with cases of fatality, it is no longer res integra that the above principles apply to cases of injury also.

Recourse can be had to Yadava Kumar v National Insurance Co Ltd. (2010) 10 SCC 341 wherein it has been ordained as thus:
"9.The Second Schedule under Section 163- A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 gives a structured formula for the calculation of compensation in accident cases.

and percentage of loss of earning capacity shall be as per Schedule I under Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923."

Thus, the multiplier method is to be applied in cases of injuries also and it has been applied in a number of accident cases by the High Courts and this Court.

As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability in the accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
14.In the present case, not only the FIR was registered and charge sheet was filed qua respondent no 1 driver u/s 279/338 IPC in the Court.
Thus, a presumption of negligence exists qua the driver respondent.
The said fact is also clear from the site plan filed along with the charge sheet.
18. Therefore, from the material on record, it is clear that the firstly the offending vehicle was taking right cut from an unauthorized point and secondly the offending vehicle had applied sudden break which led to the accident.
The fact that the the driver was doing duty beyond his working hours cannot be ignored as the fatigue may impact driver's concentration and agility.
ii. Preponderance of probabilities:
19.It is trite law that in a proceeding before the Claims Tribunal, the claimant does not have to establish negligence on the part of the driver respondent beyond reasonable doubt.
The standards of establishing negligence is predicated on preponderance of probabilities.
In the present case too, negligence has been established on this principle.
Khushbuddin vs Anil Kumar (Govt. Vehicle) on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137585863/
5
In this context, it would be useful to peruse Mathew Alexander v. Mohd. Shafi,
(2023) 13 SCC 510 wherein it was observed as thus:
"In this context, we could refer to the judgments of this Court in N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd.
v. M. Karumai Ammal [N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M. Karumai Ammal, (1980) 3 SCC 457 : 1980 SCC (Cri) 774] , wherein the plea that the criminal case had ended in acquittal and that, therefore, the civil suit must follow suit, was rejected.
The law has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 .
The gist DAR No. 781/2017 Page. 11 of 32 Khushbuddin Vs Anil Kumar & Ors of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
24. In Raj Kumar v Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 the heads under which compensation is to be calculated was expounded as thus :
[See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .]"
Recourse can be had to Yadava Kumar v National Insurance Co Ltd. (2010) 10 SCC 341 wherein it has been ordained as thus:
"9.The Second Schedule under Section 163- A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 gives a structured formula for the calculation of compensation in accident cases.
Thus, the multiplier method is to be applied in cases of injuries also and it has been applied in a number of accident cases by the High Courts and this Court.
10. This Court in Sunil Kumar v. Ram Singh Gaud [(2007) 14 SCC 61 : (2009) 1 SCC (Cri) 771 :
(2008) 1 ACJ 9] , awarded compensation in case of injury for loss of future earnings and applied the multiplier method for calculation of the same.
The same principle was recognised by this Court in Priya Vasant Kalgutkar v. Murad Shaikh [(2009) 15 SCC 54 : (2010) 2 SCC (Cri) 266 : AIR 2010 SC 40]"
27.
As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability in the accident.
This Tribunal is conscious of the fact that no amount of money can erase the trauma and grief that the victim has suffered, or the dignity and confidence that was shattered.
It was contended by Ld Counsel for the respondent insurance company that the amount of interest ought to at @7.5%, in accordance with the general prevalent practice in Courts.
